subject: Staffers at tech giants knew AI tools posed ‘existential threat’ to news publishers: court docs
posts:
Tech giants pushed AI scraping while staffers warned of an existential crisis for publishers.
Evidence: internal warnings, unsealed docs, traffic drops
#Aletheia #Tech #AI

Tech firms maintained that scraping web content for AI training constitutes protected fair use without harming the underlying media ecosystem.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Internal documents revealed executives knew AI models would cannibalize publisher traffic and threaten their economic survival.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.80) — Deception

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Tech giants pursued systematic labor extraction while hiding behind legal pretexts of transformative fair use.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.2, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- OpenAI Execution: FAIL (-0.90, -0.85) — Skirted paywalls despite internal alarms.
- Microsoft Strategy: FAIL (-0.80, -0.75) — Admitted doom loop while defending use.
Newly unsealed court documents from copyright lawsuits reveal that tech executives were well aware their AI products would siphon publisher traffic.

The Poison:
Short-term AI growth built on uncompensated extraction hollows out the journalism required to fuel future models.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (transformative technology) with WHO (labor theft from essential suppliers). Executives deployed legal pretexts to mask extraction.

Social Physics Analysis:
Tech actors ran a Smart Selfish Maneuver, harvesting proprietary labor under the pretext of fair innovation while projecting blame onto open web norms.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Hidden extraction replaces transparent partnership.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI scraping systems knowingly degrade the economic foundations of original content creators.

The Unavoidable Lie: Massive automated content harvesting constitutes benign, traditional fair use.

Alethekanon:
When corporate actors weaponize legal definitions to obscure systematic labor extraction, structural deception becomes standard operating procedure.

Journalists pour their hearts into reporting truth, only to see their life's work harvested behind closed doors without a seat at the table.

Classic tech move: admit it's a disaster internally, then lawyer up and call it fair use in public.

Ignoring the fair compensation of creators builds empires on hollow foundations.
